title: The .NET Build and Execution Model
summary: Create a .NET console project and understand source, compilation, assemblies, the runtime, entry points, diagnostics, and repeatable builds.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply The .NET Build and Execution Model
Use compiler and runtime evidence to test the contract
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: The .NET SDK supplies `dotnet new`, `dotnet build`, `dotnet run`, and testing tools. C# source is compiled into an assembly containing intermediate language and metadata; the .NET runtime loads and executes it. A project file selects the target framework and dependencies. Treat warnings as design feedback, enable nullable analysis, and read the earliest relevant diagnostic rather than changing unrelated code. `dotnet run` builds when needed, but explicit `dotnet build` is useful when separating compiler evidence from runtime behavior.
keyPoints: The .NET SDK supplies `dotnet new`, `dotnet build`, `dotnet run`, and testing tools.
commonMistakes: a runtime-only installation may not include build tools
an assembly is not raw C# source

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Add the example to a console project.
2. Predict types and output.
3. Build with warnings enabled.
4. Fix one cause at a time.
5. Run the program.
6. Add boundary tests.
